_note: Narration script for the Nausea and vomiting module (CPP-047-AO v2.3). Lee voice on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences. The prompt sent to ElevenLabs starts with the [calmly] tag and spells EOC as "E O C", ODT as "O D T" and QT as "Q T"; captions use the text here.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Why treat it
sentences: Vomiting can be a sign of something serious.
Controlling it helps comfort, and makes transport safer.
Consider ondansetron for uncontrolled nausea and vomiting, or to make transport safe.

lines.head: Take care
sentences: A long QT. AF or heart failure. Or low magnesium or potassium.
One precaution? Confirm it with the patient.
More than one? Consult the EOC Clinician.

lines.head: Giving it
sentences: Put the tablet on top of the tongue.

lines.head: Still vomiting?
sentences: For adults, they may advise a second 4 milligram dose.
And remember, it won't help motion sickness.
